data.title: GSK, Moderna settle patent dispute over Moderna COVID, RSV shots
data.description:
By Blake Brittain

British drugmaker GSK has settled lawsuits that accused Moderna's COVID-19 vaccines Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE and RSV shot mResvia of infringing its patents, the companies said on Friday.

  • Moderna said in a Friday press release that it settled GSK's patent litigation in the US and Europe on October 28 and that the companies "granted patent cross-licenses in the field of infectious disease and are not obligated to make payments of any kind in connection with such licenses."

  • A GSK spokesperson said the company was "pleased to have reached a resolution that provides clarity for both companies and enables continued focus on advancing innovation for patients."

  • The companies asked a Delaware federal court on Friday to dismiss GSK's US infringement claims with prejudice, which means they cannot be refiled

  • GSK sued Moderna in 2024 over lipid nanoparticle technology used in the vaccines to transport fragile messenger RNA (mRNA) into the human body

  • GSK separately filed a similar lawsuit against Pfizer and BioNTech over their COVID-19 vaccine earlier that year, which is still ongoing

  • The lawsuits are part of a web of US court cases involving Pfizer, BioNTech and Moderna over patent royalties for technology used in their COVID vaccines, including one brought by Moderna against Pfizer in 2022

data.title: Mississippi US Senate candidates battle over ballots as winner remains unclear
data.description:
Key points:
  • Colom leads Hyde-Smith 49.0% to 48.8%, Reuters/USA Today vote counts show
  • About 12,000 to 20,000 provisional ballots remain to be counted
  • Mississippi is the only US state without a recount provision

By Leah Douglas

US Senate candidates in Mississippi are battling over the treatment of ballots still being counted in the race, one of two remaining Senate contests yet to be called after Tuesday's midterm elections.

The outcome in Mississippi and in Alaska, where the Senate race is also not yet called, will determine whether the Democratic Party extends its sweeping election victory in which it seized at least 54 of the Senate's 100 seats, and also took control of the US House of Representatives.

Democrat Scott Colom narrowly leads incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by 49.0% to 48.8%, according to vote counts compiled by Reuters and USA Today, which are partnering this year to collect live election results for Senate and House races.

Hyde-Smith sent a letter on Thursday to all 82 Mississippi county election commissioners demanding that their offices preserve all affidavit, or provisional, ballots and separate them from regular and absentee ballots.

"These measures are necessary to ensure that each affidavit ballot's eligibility for counting and ultimate disposition can be verified," said the letter from law firm Lex Politica, which represents Hyde-Smith.

Colom sent a letter later in the day to the commissioners calling Hyde-Smith's request unlawful, in part because it could result in different treatment of ballots across counties.

Departing from normal election procedures would be a violation of Mississippi election law, said the letter from Elias Law Group, which represents Colom.

"I have faith that the process will be followed correctly, and everybody just needs to calm down, follow the law," Colom said to reporters on Friday, expressing confidence that he would win the race. "The people of Mississippi have spoken. We all know where this is going."

Affidavit ballots, which require extra review because of questions about voter eligibility, could determine the outcome of the race. Between 12,000 and 20,000 remain to be counted, Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson said on Thursday.

If Colom wins, he would be the first Black US senator elected from Mississippi since 1874.

Democrats' midterm victories were propelled by widespread discontent with President Donald Trump's policies, and the party will control Congress when the new session starts in January.

Mississippi counties have 10 days from Election Day, or until November 13, to submit certified election results.

It is the only US state without a legal provision for vote recounts in statewide elections. Candidates could pursue a legal challenge to exclude certain ballots, which could change the vote count.

data.title: Fall in the euro supports EU wheat
data.description:
European wheat rose on Friday, helped by a fall in the euro making European grains more competitive on the world market while traders continued to focus on the situation in the Black Sea and strong shipments out of France.

Benchmark December milling wheat on Paris-based Euronext, closed the daily session 0.9% higher at €225.00 ($250.88) a metric ton. Further deliveries were slightly lower.

One trader pointed to fund buying to explain the rise in the contract spread.

The US dollar jumped on Friday and was on pace for its biggest daily percentage gain in seven weeks as it extended gains after a stronger-than-expected US payrolls report.

Euronext said on Friday it will launch Black Sea wheat and corn futures next year with physical delivery to the port of Constanta in Romania to expand its European grain business, which has historically been tied to France.

The exchange has long sought ways to reflect rising Black Sea grain trade, including previous plans to add delivery in Romania to its existing French-based corn contract .

French farmers had sown 84% of this year's soft wheat crop by November 2, up from 62% a week earlier and 77% a year ago, farm office FranceAgriMer said on Friday.

This year's French grain maize harvest was now over, compared with 99% complete a week earlier, the farm office said.

World food prices edged lower in October as weaker import demand contributed to monthly declines in cereal, dairy and meat prices, but were still nearly 6% higher than a year earlier, the UN Food and Agriculture Organization said on Friday.

FAO's cereal price index fell 4.5% from September and was 12.6% lower than a year ago, as wheat and maize quotations declined. Wheat prices eased on weak import demand and improved production prospects, especially in Argentina, it said.

data.title: Extreme Networks Shares Jump on Report of Sale Process
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Shares of Extreme Networks rose after Reuters reported that the networking software and equipment company is exploring a sale.

Shares were up 13% at $23.70 on Friday. The stock has gained 42% this year.

The company has engaged an investment bank for a sale process, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Possible strategic buyers could be Fortinet, Cisco and NetApp, according to the report.

Extreme Networks and NetApp declined to comment to Reuters, while Cisco and Fortinet didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Microsoft winds down rented AI computing capacity from Oracle: report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Microsoft is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle , Bloomberg News reported on Friday.
  • Microsoft has been turning off rented computing capacity from Oracle in recent months after declining to renew the contract, according to the report.
  • The computing capacity had become less useful because it no longer met Microsoft's requirements. The Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia chips, the people said.
  • The agreement, announced in 2023, involved Oracle providing Microsoft access to servers that would power a new AI-assisted version of its Bing search engine. The full value of the deal is not public.
  • Microsoft also decided against expanding its computing agreement with British AI cloud provider Nscale at a Texas data center. The potential extension would have been worth tens of billions of dollars to Nscale .
  • Microsoft has been taking a more cautious approach to renting computing capacity from third-party AI providers, amid concerns about project delays, regulatory hurdles, and rising costs. The company is also directing more spending toward expanding its data center capacity.

data.title: IDBI Bank stake sale: 'Very, very remote' chance of finding another buyer at Rs.52,000 crore, says DIPAM Secretary Chawla
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 6 -- The government opted to continue with the IDBI Bank disinvestment exercise by giving bidders another opportunity to improve their offers, rather than abandoning the existing process, DIPAM Secretary Arunish Chawla said. He clarified that the reserve price remained unchanged throughout the exercise.

During a conversation with CNBC-TV18, Chawla described the chances of attracting a fresh buyer prepared to pay Rs.52,000 crore for the combined government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) stakes as "very, very remote".

He stated the authorities weighed three alternatives - cancelling the initial bidding exercise, accepting the offer already received, and inviting improved bids - before the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) settled on seeking revised or best offers to maximise the transaction value.

Chawla explained that the subsequent bidding exercise differed from the initial round because all parties involved were already aware of the price discovered during the first phase.

He said strategic disinvestment deals are not conducted like regular auctions with a fixed reserve-price threshold against which every bid is evaluated.

Rejecting the view that offers below the reserve price are automatically ineligible for approval, Chawla pointed to the Paradeep Phosphates privatisation, where the accepted offer was 15% lower than the reserve price.

He further said the revised offer exceeded the fair-value assessments as well as their average. The Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) unanimously considered the improved bid reasonable, he added.

Chawla said the government introduced an income-tax indemnity capped at Rs.627 crore for the bidders, a provision that contributed to a Rs.3,917-crore increase in the bid value.

He mentioned the decision was based on the overall financial gains expected to accrue to the government and LIC from the transaction, rather than viewing the reserve price as a rigid benchmark.

Chawla reiterated that the reserve price remained unchanged throughout the bidding exercise and was neither revised nor fixed again.

On October 14, the government cleared the proposed sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings for approximately Rs.53,000 crore ($5.5 billion). The deal, if completed, would mark the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank and a significant step forward in the country's long-pending banking privatisation programme.

The strategic disinvestment is targeted for completion by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
